method: One ordinary-O3 executable receives iteration counts 100 and 10000. Each iteration exercises eight caught failures during partially evaluated calls, construction, containers, string concatenation, and a chained comparison. DHAT measures requested live heap and allocation traffic, not RSS or allocator-reserved memory. Profiling runs after all wall-time comparisons; diagnostic durations are not performance results.
derivation: Start from dedented ACCEPTED['partial_construction']; replace the sole range(100) loop with an input-driven iterations local and range(iterations); replace the fixed success text with recovered plus the actual iteration count. The same generated binary is used for both inputs.

dhat_trace_normalization: Complete DHAT JSON is embedded for each run. Absolute repository and profiler paths are replaced by public placeholders; every allocation counter is unchanged. normalized_dhat_trace_sha256 hashes UTF-8 json.dumps(trace, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon)); raw_files.trace.sha256 identifies the original unmodified trace bytes.
conclusion: Both runs have 18140 peak live requested bytes in 14 blocks and 17408 end-live bytes in three persistent I/O buffers. Traffic scales with recovery count without growth in these live-heap measurements; this is bounded evidence for the exercised paths, not a universal leak proof.
